goldenPlover: In Iceland her return is news: the first lóa of the year means spring has arrived.
Icelanders hear her call as “dýrðin, dýrðin”, the glory.
Many Icelandic golden plovers spend the winter in Britain and Ireland.
sparklingVioletear: In Ecuador hummingbirds are called quindes, a word that comes from Kichwa.
The sparkling violetear is one of the most common hummingbirds in Quito's gardens.
Ecuador is home to more than 130 hummingbird species.
ceret: Every spring the first cherries in France come from Céret and are sent to the President of the Republic.
In the early 20th century Picasso, Braque and Juan Gris spent seasons in Céret, which is why it is called the Mecca of Cubism.
Céret's 14th-century Pont du Diable crosses the river Tech in a single arch of about 45 metres.
france: France is the most visited country in the world.
Counting its overseas territories, France spans 12 time zones, more than any other country.
Because of its shape, the French call their country “the Hexagon”.
reykjavik: Reykjavík is the northernmost capital of a sovereign state.
Its name means “smoky bay”, after the steam rising from the hot springs.
Almost every house in Reykjavík is heated with geothermal energy.
iceland: Iceland's Alþingi, founded in 930, is one of the oldest parliaments in the world.
There are no mosquitoes in Iceland.
More than half of Icelanders live in and around Reykjavík.
